To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

AADC cells in the spinal dorsal horn are a source of 5-HT, DA and NA, that AADC cells in spinal ventral horns are a potential source of DA and NA, and that AADC cells are also a source of the catecholamine precursor, L-DOPA.
the AADC cells in the spinal dorsal horn and intermediate zone express 5-HT and DA, and that they are capable of producing these two monoamines.
AADC cells are present in the mammalian spinal gray matter, they are capable of synthesizing monoamines, and they are the most likely origin of residual monoamines after spinal transection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of monoamines in the spinal cord, especially the origin of residual monoamines in the injured spinal cord.
the origin of monoamine neurotransmitters in the spinal cord, especially the residual monoamines cauda to the lesion.
a novel population of AADC cells that are widely distributed throughout the spinal cord, and are the most numerous of all intraspinal monoamine cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AADC cells, but not intraspinal monoamine-producing cells, are the source of residual monoamine neurotransmitters in spinal cord below a complete spinal transection.

intraspinal 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA) is the major source of residual DA in the spinal cord after transection, whereas intraspinal 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate is the major source for residual NA and 5-HT.
intraspinal AADC cells are the source of monoamines in the spinal cord.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AADC cells in the rat spinal cord express the enzyme AADC, which catalyses the conversion of L-tyrosine to DA and of 5-HTP to 5-HT.

(1) AADC, the rate-limiting enzyme in the synthesis of monoamines, occurs in spinal cord astrocytes; (2) AADC is localized to the cytosol and nucleus of spinal cord astrocyte; (3) AADC expression in spinal cord astroglial cells is regulated at the transcriptional level; (4) AADC is expressed in the spinal cord of all mammals studied; (5) AADC expression is increased in the spinal cord following SCI;
the AADC is a key enzyme in the biosynthesis of catecholamines, DA and NA, and serotonin (5-HT).
The main takeaway from our work is that
AADC, a key enzyme for the synthesis of monoamines, is expressed in a subpopulation of spinal cord neurons.
AADC, which is an enzyme responsible for converting 5-HTP to 5-HT and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine to DA, is present in a population of cells in the spinal gray matter.
the spinal AADC cells are not only the major source of the residual 5-HT and NA, but also the major source of DA.
